Alice H: Quick check-in — I ran a short real-world QPS check comparing A100 vs H100 for Llama-2-7b (q4_nf4) across us-west-2 and eu-central-1. Focused on prefill p50/p95, decode tokens/sec, and $/1M tokens. High-level: H100 wins on decode throughput and cost when you need low latency; A100 still competitive if you can batch.
Ben R: Nice. Can you drop the raw numbers and what kernel/quant configs you used?
Alice H: Yep. Setup: 1k short conversations sampled from prod prompt set. Prefill=512 tokens, decode=256 tokens, batching tuned to keep latency SLOs.
Carla S: Commands:

```
run_bench --model llama-2-7b --quant q4_nf4 --gpu {A100|H100} --region {us-west-2,eu-central-1} \
  --batch 8 --prefill 512 --decode 256 --samples 1000 --kernels flash_attn2,triton
```
Carla S: Raw summary (median and 95th pcts, tokens/sec measured during decode phase):

```
GPU   REGION       PREFILL_p50  PREFILL_p95  DECODE_tok/s  $/1M_tokens  GPU_mem
A100  us-west-2    180 ms       420 ms       1200 t/s      $20          10.8 GB
A100  eu-central-1 200 ms       460 ms       1100 t/s      $21          10.8 GB
H100  us-west-2    150 ms       330 ms       2100 t/s      $12          11.2 GB
H100  eu-central-1 165 ms       350 ms       2000 t/s      $13          11.2 GB
```
Ryan M: Notes: kernels used were flash_attn2 for attention + triton fused kernels for MLP. For A100 we fell back to a slower matmul path for some shapes — that explains part of prefill p95 delta. Batch size 8 was tuned to keep p95 under ~500ms on A100.
Meera P: What about quantization quality? Any regression vs baseline fp16?
Alice H: Quick eval on a 200-shot conv test: q4_nf4 moves exact-match pass rate by ~0.7% absolute vs fp16 on our prompt set (tiny). Perplexity up ~1.2%. For our production thresholds that's acceptable but flagging it in the rollout.
Ben R: How did you compute $/1M tokens? Does that include overhead (CPU, region price diff)?
Carla S: Back-of-envelope: used per-hour instance price * effective tokens/sec during steady-state decode, then scaled. Included instance-hour + networking egress estimate. We quoted region-adjusted vCPU+GPU market price (spot-equivalent removed for P50). Example calc: cost = price_per_hour / (tokens_per_sec * 3600) * 1e6.
Ryan M: A few micro observations:
- KV cache warmup affects prefill: repeated prefixes get ~25% lower prefill p50 on H100 because KV IO was faster.
- For long-prefill scenarios (>1024) H100 advantages grow.
Meera P: Any kernel/compilation tricks that mattered?
Carla S: Yes — enabling fused rotary kernels + prefetch in Triton improved A100 decode by ~10%. On H100, enabling cuda graph capture + persistent kernels reduced tail latency. We also tested flash_attn v2 vs v3; v3 reduced memory but sometimes increased p95 on A100.
deploy-bot: deploy/test-runner started for region eu-central-1 (job id jd-9982)
Alice H: Practical recommendation for sizing given these results:
- If you need <10ms per-token decode tail and <200ms prefill p95 for 7b conversational flows, prefer H100 Dedicated or H100-backed nodes.
- If your workload can batch to 16+ and tolerate a p95 ~450-600ms, A100 offers lower capital cost, especially if you use aggressive batching + fused kernels.
- For multi-region redundancy: place primary read in region with lowest egress cost; replicate KV cache to reduce inter-region cold prefill spikes.
Ben R: For a target footprint: say 500 QPS with avg 40 decode tokens per request — rough instance counts?
Carla S: Quick calc: 500 QPS * 40 toks = 20k tps. Using tokens/sec from table:
- H100: 2000 t/s per GPU -> need ~10 GPUs (plus 20% headroom -> 12)
- A100: 1100 t/s per GPU -> need ~19 GPUs (plus 20% headroom -> 23)
Cost-wise that matches the $/1M extrapolation above.
Meera P: Also add eval gating for any quant rollout. 0.5-1% quality delta should go through stricter A/B with production prompts.
Alice H: I'll draft a short PR with the raw CSV, scripts, and a recommendation for Dedicated vs Reserved capacity. Thanks for the quick feedback :thumbsup:
Ryan M: LGTM — if you push the CSV I can add kernel flags we toggled.
Carla S: Pushed results to the bench bucket: s3://redwood-bench/realworld-qps/1990012345/ — contains raw logs + summary.csv
Alice H: Perfect. Closing this thread; will open a follow-up for 13B when we have enough credits to run the same matrix.
